data.title: Integration Test
data.tagline: An integration test verifies that multiple modules or dependencies cooperate correctly.
data.learningOutcome: You can see a cross-module failure as a reason to inspect connections, fields, and data transfer rather than only one function.
data.description: A registration form sends a name to an API, the API writes a database, then returns success or error to the page. This finds mismatched field names, formats, and error handoff. A pure calculation function with fixed input remains a unit test.

learning.assumes: You know a page, API, and database can divide one save operation.
learning.outcome: You can see a cross-module failure as a reason to inspect connections, fields, and data transfer rather than only one function.

distinctions.label: End-to-end test
distinctions.explanation: An Integration Test focuses on the connection between selected modules. An End-to-End Test drives the whole system from a user entry point to a visible result.

explanation.title: Handoffs create unique failures
explanation.text: A page can send `startDate` while a server expects `start_date`; each unit may work alone but fail together. Integration tests check requests, responses, and formats across neighboring modules.

explanation.title: Errors travel through the connection too
explanation.text: When the server rejects a registration, the page should show a useful reason. Checking only a successful write misses whether failure information reaches the right interface.

data.boundary: An integration test is not running the whole product. It selects cooperating modules and dependencies; a full journey from browser entry to a visible result is an end-to-end test.

lessonPractice.title: Price unit tests pass, but the total is blank after form submission. What best follows integration-test thinking?

options.label: Submit the form and check that its total field, the API response field, and the page field agree
options.feedback: Correct. Each small unit may be right on its own; the data contract at their handoff is often wrong.

options.label: Add more input combinations to the price function and confirm it still returns a total on its own
options.feedback: That strengthens the unit test but does not check whether the total moves correctly through the form, API, and page.

options.label: Complete a real payment in the browser and only check whether the final confirmation page has an amount
options.feedback: A full user flow can prove the result, but its scope is wider. With unit evidence already available, checking the adjacent handoffs will locate the issue faster.

data.agentPrompt: Run an integration test for registration saving: check form request fields, API input and response fields, database write, and whether server errors appear on the form. Report one valid and one invalid-input result afterward.
